links.reason: The consumer expressly uses the finite bilinear/quadratic alphabet supplied here. It forms coordinate powers and additive orthogonal codes on the same Q/Z-valued carrier. The finite-cardinality and double-perpendicular conclusions require a nondegenerate polar form: the unrestricted formula is H-perp-perp = H + rad(b), not H. Field-linear Euclidean and Hermitian code duals still require the separate field-to-additive pairing comparisons owned by coding theory; no Hermitian structure is supplied by a symmetric Q/Z pairing.

evidence.quote:
Define a finite bilinear module as a finite abelian group with a symmetric biadditive
  `ℚ/ℤ`-valued form.

For a finite bilinear alphabet `A` from the integral-lattices roadmap, construct the coordinate
  power on `ι → A` by summing pairings. Define the orthogonal additive code and prove the
  finite-cardinality and double-perpendicular results under nondegeneracy.

links.reason: Construction A needs the shared full rational lattice with its integral symmetric form and invariants. For m >= 2 and an additive code C, first construct the full preimage carrier in Q^ι with B_m(x,y) = (sum x_i*y_i)/m; only after proving C <= C-perp may it be bundled as IntegralLattice. Layer 1 supplies that bundle, the integral/rational comparison, evenness, unimodularity and isometry vocabulary. Coding theory owns the residue calculation, its literal dual-carrier identity and the proof of the required integrality. No square root is introduced into the rational ambient space, and no nonintegral code preimage is treated as an integral lattice.

evidence.quote:
Define an integral symmetric lattice from a carrier `L : Submodule ℤ V` with
  `[L.IsLattice ℚ]`, a symmetric `B : BilinForm ℚ V`, and a proof that `B(L,L)⊆ℤ`.

Prove that `P_m(C)` is a full `ℤ`-lattice in `ℚ^ι` for every `C`.  It bundles as an
  `IntegralLattice` exactly when `C ≤ C^⊥`.

links.reason: The nondegenerate integral branch of Construction A uses the canonical dual lattice, discriminant and unimodularity criteria. Once coding theory proves its literal equality P_m(C)^dual = P_m(C-perp), the equivalence of self-duality, trivial discriminant and unimodularity is the Layer-2 lattice theorem applied on that carrier. B_m is positive definite for m > 0; integrality additionally requires C <= C-perp. The direct dual-preimage calculation for arbitrary additive C remains in coding theory, because the nonintegral branch is not an input to the bundled Layer-2 theorem.

evidence.quote:
Prove the equivalence of the following, with nondegeneracy, integrality, fullness, and finite rank
  visible in the theorem context: `L=L^∨`; `A_L` is trivial; `#A_L=1`; the Gram determinant has
  absolute value one; and the restricted pairing `L → Module.Dual ℤ L` is an equivalence.

Prove that integral `P_m(C)` is unimodular exactly when `C=C^⊥`.  Keep self-orthogonality visible
  in the construction so “unimodular” is never asserted of an unbundled nonintegral carrier.

links.reason: The coordinate discriminant bridge has to start from the actual subtype quotient L0^dual/L0 and its canonical bilinear form, not an abstract finite group of the same order. Layer 2 supplies this quotient, representative API and form. Coding theory identifies L0=m Z^ι in (Q^ι,B_m), computes L0^dual=Z^ι and proves the reduction-modulo-m isometry. Thus m need not be prime and field-linearity is not assumed. The even quadratic refinement uses Layer 3 separately.

evidence.quote:
Define `A_L` as the actual quotient of the subtype `L^∨` by the inverse-image of `L`; provide its
  quotient map, representative lemmas, zero criterion, additive-group structure, and functorial map
  induced by an isometry.

Let `L₀(m,ι)` have carrier `mℤ^ι` in `ℚ^ι` and form `B_m`.  Prove
  `L₀(m,ι)^∨=ℤ^ι` and construct an isometry
  `A_{L₀} ≅ (ZMod m)^ι` carrying the class of an integer vector to its coordinatewise
  reduction modulo `m`, and carrying the discriminant pairing to
  `∑ lift(x_i)lift(y_i)/m mod ℤ`.

links.reason: The bridge transports coordinate quadratic forms to actual lattice discriminant forms and takes orthogonal sums. Layer 3 supplies the half-norm Q/Z discriminant quadratic module, sum isometries and polar-form API. Coding theory supplies the specific coordinate isometries and checks isotropy of the named codes. For L0(m,ι), the quadratic refinement is used only for even m; an odd integral lattice has a discriminant bilinear module but not this canonical quadratic refinement. The common q=B(x,x)/2 convention must be retained for A2 and D4 as well.

evidence.quote:
For an even lattice,
  prove `B(x,x)/2 mod ℤ` descends to `A_L`, has polar form `b_L`, and is nondegenerate; package it as
  its discriminant quadratic module.

State the reusable interface for an isometry from a coordinate finite quadratic module to the
  discriminant module of an orthogonal lattice sum.  Its input subgroup remains an
  `AddSubgroup`; field-linearity is used only when separately proved for a named code.

links.reason: This is an expressly delegated gluing theorem, not duplicate mathematics: after coding theory constructs the coordinate discriminant isometry and transports C as an actual subgroup, use the intermediate-overlattice correspondence and A_(L_H) isometric to H-perp/H. Bilinear isotropy gives integrality; quadratic isotropy gives evenness when the original lattice is even. Transport the isometry to P_m(C), including the actual quotient and representative map, and derive unimodularity from the Lagrangian condition. Neither the determinant formula alone nor matching abstract group orders supplies this conclusion.

evidence.quote:
For isotropic `H`, define the induced form on `H^⊥/H` and construct the natural isometry
  `A_{L_H} ≅ H^⊥/H`, bilinear in the integral case and quadratic in the even case.

Consume the general gluing theorem to obtain, for isotropic `C`, the natural isometry
  `A_{P_m(C)} ≅ C^⊥/C`, first as an isometry of finite bilinear modules and, when `m` is even
  and `q_m|_C=0`, as an isometry of finite quadratic modules.

links.reason: Layer 5 supplies actual finite quadratic modules of A2 and D4 with the chosen positive root-norm-two convention. Coding theory transports them to additive GF(3) and GF(4) coordinate alphabets. For A2 specialize q=n/(2(n+1)) at n=2, obtaining q(1)=1/3 and b(a,b)=2ab/3 modulo Z. For D4 the vector and two spinor classes all have q=1/2; their polar pairing is the half trace-Hermitian pairing after the explicitly named GF(4) identification. The supplier must give the named generators, pairings and isometries, not only groups Z/3 and (Z/2)^2. Coordinate summation, trace-Hermitian versus Hermitian duality for GF(4)-linear codes, isotropy of a particular code and its glued lattice remain coding theory. No classification of unimodular lattices follows just from these values.

evidence.quote: | `D_n`, even `n≥4` | `(ℤ/2)²` | vector class has `q=1/2`; both spinor classes have `q=n/8`. |

Use the `A_2` discriminant generator of squared norm `2/3` to transport its quadratic module to
  the additive group of `GF(3)`, with
  `q(a)=lift(a)^2/3 mod ℤ` and `b(a,b)=2 lift(a)lift(b)/3 mod ℤ`.

Use the three nonzero `D_4` discriminant classes (vector and both spinors) to identify the
  additive group with `GF(4)`, taking `1` to the vector class and `ω,ω²` to the spinor classes.

overlaps.detail: GN.2 says to add integral lattices while the completed upstream roadmap already owns full rational symmetric integral lattices, integral isometries and their basic invariant API. That common rational/Z symmetric subcase is an ownership overlap. It is not an overlap with the entire quaternionic or hermitian theory, nor does it make integral genus classification an upstream theorem.
overlaps.proposal: Retain the canonical rational/Z symmetric lattice bundle and its signature, dual and finite-discriminant interfaces in IntegralLattices. Make GN.2 import it for that subcase, with comparison maps if its broader arithmetic base uses a different carrier. Keep genera, spinor genera, local classification, hermitian/quaternionic coefficients and their hypotheses in GN.2. No whole-roadmap merge and no directed prerequisite for the duplicate construction are asserted before this boundary is reconciled.
